title: Top 10 Tourist Places Near Delhi Metro Stations (With Exit Numbers)
tags: Places to visit near metro stations
description: Discover the top 10 tourist places near Delhi Metro stations with exact exit gate numbers. Step-by-step guide to Red Fort, India Gate, Akshardham & more. Walking distance, time-saving tips, and a map included for budget travel.
body:
Planning a trip to Delhi and wondering how to reach the Red Fort by metro or which exit gate to use at the Chandni Chowk metro station? You're in the right place!

[Delhi Metro](https://metroguideindia.com/delhi-metro/) is not just a commute system; it's your ticket to effortless Delhi sightseeing. With over 285+ stations across 12 lines, the metro connects you to walking distance tourist attractions, saves you from traffic hell, and keeps your budget intact.

This step-by-step guide reveals the top 10 tourist places near Delhi Metro stations with exact exit gate numbers, walking directions, quick tips, and time-saving hacks that locals use. No more confusion at metro exits, no wasted time searching for the right gate, and no expensive auto rides.

Whether you're looking for Delhi tourist places near the Yellow Line metro, tourist attractions on the Delhi Metro Blue Line, or simply the nearest metro station to India Gate with gate number, this guide has everything you need for budget travel in Delhi.

Map included in each section to help you visualize the route!

***

## Why This Guide Is Different: Exact Exit Gates, Not Just Station Names

Most travel blogs tell you the nearest metro station, but **that's not enough**. At busy stations like Rajiv Chowk or Kashmere Gate, there are **5–7 exit gates**, and using the wrong one can add 10–15 minutes of unnecessary walking.

This guide gives you:

- ✅ **Exact exit gate numbers** for each tourist place
- ✅ **Walking distance** from gate to attraction (in minutes)
- ✅ **Step-by-step directions** to avoid confusion
- ✅ **Quick tips** for Yulu bikes, auto stands, and shortcuts
- ✅ **Best time to visit** and entry fee details
- ✅ **Metro line information** for route planning

Perfect for first-time visitors, solo travelers, families, and anyone doing **Delhi sightseeing by metro**.

***

## 1. India Gate

> The Iconic War Memorial & National Landmark

![India Gate evening ](/assets/images/blog/India%20Gate.jpg "India Gate")

India Gate is Delhi's most iconic monument, a 42-meter-high war memorial commemorating 82,000+ Indian soldiers who died in World War I. The newly renovated **Kartavya Path** makes it a must-visit for every tourist.

| Detail | Information |
| **Nearest Metro Station** | [Central Secretariat](https://metroguideindia.com/delhi-metro/stations/central-secretariat.html) (Yellow Line + Violet Line) |
| **Best Exit Gate** | **Gate No. 3** (towards India Gate/Kartavya Path) |
| **Walking Distance** | 10-minute walk (800 meters) along Kartavya Path |
| **Alternative Gate** | Gate No. 4 (slightly longer, 12-minute walk) |
| **Metro Line** | Yellow Line (Samaypur Badli to R.K. Puram) + Violet Line (Kashmere Gate to Raja Nahar Singh) |
| **Quick Tip** | Exit from Gate 3 to easily find a **Yulu bike hub** right outside if you prefer riding over walking! Yulu charges ₹20–₹40 for short rides. |

### Step-by-Step Walking Directions from Gate 3

1. Exit through **Gate No. 3** at Central Secretariat metro station
2. Walk straight towards **Rashtrapati Bhavan** direction
3. Cross the road safely at the designated pedestrian crossing
4. You'll see the **renovated Kartavya Path** ahead
5. Walk straight for 800 meters, India Gate will be directly in front of you
6. The path is well-lit, shaded, and **pedestrian-friendly**

### Best Time to Visit

- **Morning:** 6:00 AM – 9:00 AM (cooler, less crowded)
- **Evening:** 5:00 PM – 9:00 PM (beautiful sunset views, night illumination)
- **Avoid:** Midday (11 AM – 4 PM) due to heat

### Entry Fee

- **Free** (no entry charge)
- Light and sound show: ₹60 adults, ₹30 children (evening only)

### Why This Is Perfect for Metro Tourists

India Gate is at **walking distance** from Central Secretariat, making it one of the easiest **Delhi Metro tourist places** to visit. The **Yellow Line** connects you from airport (via interchange) to this iconic spot.

***

## 2. Red Fort (Lal Qila)

> UNESCO World Heritage Site & Mughal Marvel

![Red Fort main entrance with metro station in background](/assets/images/blog/Red%20Fort.jpg "Red Fort main entrance with metro station in background")

The **Red Fort** is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the **best tourist places in Delhi**. Built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in 1648, this massive red sandstone fort houses palaces, audience halls, and museums.

| Detail | Information |
| **Nearest Metro Station** | [**Chandni Chowk Metro Station**](https://metroguideindia.com/delhi-metro/stations/chandni-chowk.html) (Yellow Line) |
| **Best Exit Gate** | **Gate No. 1** (directly towards Red Fort entrance) |
| **Walking Distance** | 5-minute walk (400 meters) |
| **Alternative Gate** | Gate No. 2 (6-minute walk, near Jama Masjid side) |
| **Metro Line** | Yellow Line (Samaypur Badli to R.K. Puram) |
| **Quick Tip** | Gate 1 leads directly to the **Red Fort main entrance**. Avoid Gate 3–5, they're towards the market side, adding 10+ minutes of walking. |

### Step-by-Step Walking Directions from Gate 1

1. Exit through **Gate No. 1** at Chandni Chowk metro station
2. You'll see the **Red Fort entrance** clearly visible ahead
3. Walk straight on the footpath for 400 meters
4. Cross the street at the pedestrian signal
5. You'll reach the [**Lal Qila main gate**](https://metroguideindia.com/delhi-metro/stations/lal-quila.html) (Lahori Gate) in 5 minutes
6. **Auto stands** are available if you prefer not to walk

### How to Reach Red Fort by Metro - Complete Route

### From New Delhi Railway Station

- Take Yellow Line towards Samaypur Badli
- 1 stop to Chandni Chowk
- Exit Gate 1, 5-minute walk

### From Airport (IGI Terminal 3)

- Take Airport Express to [Dhaula Kuan](https://metroguideindia.com/delhi-metro/stations/dhaula-kuan.html)
- Interchange to Yellow Line towards Samaypur Badli
- 12 stops to Chandni Chowk
- Exit Gate 1

### From Rajiv Chowk (Central Delhi)

- Take Yellow Line towards Samaypur Badli
- 4 stops to Chandni Chowk
- Exit Gate 1

### Best Time to Visit

- **Morning:** 9:00 AM – 11:00 AM (cooler, less crowded)
- **Avoid:** Mondays (closed for maintenance)
- **Evening:** 5:00 PM – 7:00 PM (beautiful lighting)

### Entry Fee

- **Indian Citizens:** ₹35
- **Foreign Tourists:** ₹550
- **Children below 15:** Free
- **Light and Sound Show:** ₹60 (evening only)

### Chandni Chowk Metro Station Exit Gate for Market

If you want to explore **Chandni Chowk market** instead of Red Fort:

- **Gate No. 3** leads directly to the main market
- **Gate No. 4** is closer to Jama Masjid
- **Gate No. 1** is best for Red Fort only

### Why Red Fort Is Perfect for Metro Tourists

The **Red Fort nearest metro station exit gate** (Gate 1) makes this **UNESCO site** incredibly accessible. This is one of the top **places to visit near metro stations** for history buffs.

## 3. Akshardham Temple

> Spiritual Marvel & Architectural Masterpiece

![Akshardham Temple complex with fountain show](/assets/images/blog/Akshardham-NewDelhi-Watershow-07-1800x1012.jpg "Akshardham Temple complex with fountain show")

**Akshardham Temple** is one of the **best tourist places in Delhi** and a spiritual masterpiece. This massive Hindu temple complex features intricate carvings, gardens, exhibitions, and a spectacular water show.

| Detail | Information |
| **Nearest Metro Station** | [**Akshardham Metro Station**](https://metroguideindia.com/delhi-metro/stations/akshardham.html) (Blue Line) |
| **Best Exit Gate** | **Gate No. 1** (directly towards temple entrance) |
| **Walking Distance** | 3-minute walk (200 meters), truly **walking distance**! |
| **Alternative Gate** | Gate No. 2 (5-minute walk, towards Yauvaraja term) |
| **Metro Line** | Blue Line (Dwarka Sector 21 to Noida Electronic City) |
| **Quick Tip** | **How to reach Akshardham temple by metro** is easiest via Gate 1, it drops you right at the temple security checkpoint. Lockers available for bags. |

### Step-by-Step Walking Directions from Gate 1

1. Exit through **Gate No. 1** at Akshardham metro station
2. Walk straight for 200 meters, you'll see the temple entrance
3. Pass through **security checkpoint** (no large bags, cameras allowed inside)
4. Enter the main temple complex
5. **Baggage locker** available outside (₹20 per bag)

### What to See Inside Akshardham

- **Main Temple:** Incredible stone carvings, no metal allowed inside
- **Yajnakund:** Fire ritual demonstration
- **Exhibition Halls:** Hindu culture, spirituality, and history
- **Boat Ride:** "Yayatra" - 17-minute journey through Indian history (₹60)
- **Water Show:** "Sandhya Raglil" - evening light and music show (₹80)
- **Garden:** Beautifully landscaped gardens (free)

### Best Time to Visit

- **Morning:** 9:00 AM – 11:00 AM (less crowded, cooler)
- **Evening:** 5:00 PM – 8:00 PM (water show at 7:00 PM)
- **Closed:** Mondays

### Entry Fee

- **Temple Complex:** Free
- **Boat Ride:** ₹60 adults, ₹30 children
- **Water Show:** ₹80 adults, ₹40 children
- **Total Experience:** ₹120–₹150 per person

### How to Reach Akshardham Temple by Metro - Complete Route

### From Rajiv Chowk

- Take Blue Line towards Noida Electronic City
- 7 stops to Akshardham
- Exit Gate 1, 3-minute walk

### From Noida

- Take Blue Line towards Dwarka Sector 21
- Direct access to Akshardham
- Exit Gate 1

### From Airport

- Take Airport Express to Rajiv Chowk
- Interchange to Blue Line towards Noida Electronic City
- 7 stops to Aksharkan
- Exit Gate 1

### Why Akshardham Is Perfect for Metro Tourists

How to reach the Akshardham temple by metro is straightforward; the station is literally named after it! This is the easiest tourist attraction on Delhi Metro Blue Line to access.

## 4. Lotus Temple (Bahá'í House of Worship)

> Architectural Wonder & Peaceful Retreat

![Lotus Temple exterior with visitors walking](/assets/images/blog/Lotus%20Temple%20exterior%20with%20visitors%20walking.webp "Lotus Temple exterior with visitors walking")

The **Lotus Temple** is one of the most **photogenic tourist places near Delhi Metro stations**. This Bahá'í House of Worship, shaped like a lotus flower, welcomes people of all faiths and offers a peaceful retreat in busy Delhi.

| Detail | Information |
| **Nearest Metro Station** | [**Kalkaji Mandir Metro Station**](https://metroguideindia.com/delhi-metro/stations/kalkaji-mandir.html) (Violet Line + Magenta Line) |
| **Best Exit Gate** | **Gate No. 2** (directly towards Lotus Temple) |
| **Walking Distance** | 7-minute walk (600 meters) |
| **Alternative Gate** | Gate No. 1 (10-minute walk, towards bus stand) |
| **Metro Line** | Violet Line (Kashmere Gate to Raja Nahar Singh) + Magenta Line (Janakpuri West to Botanical Garden) |
| **Quick Tip** | Exit Gate 2, you'll see the **Lotus Temple signage** immediately. Auto stands are available if you prefer not to walk. |

### Step-by-Step Walking Directions from Gate 2

1. Exit through **Gate No. 2** at Kalkaji Mandir metro station
2. Walk straight on the main road (Lambda Road)
3. You'll see the **Lotus Temple signage** after 200 meters
4. Turn right at the temple sign
5. Walk 400 meters on the dedicated footpathThe 
6. Lotus Temple entrance will be directly ahead

### What to Expect Inside Lotus Temple

- **Main Prayer Hall:** Open to all faiths, no religious rituals performed
- **Gardens:** Beautifully maintained, perfect for photos
- **Silence & Meditation:** Peaceful atmosphere, no talking allowed inside
- **Photography:** Allowed outside, not inside the prayer hall
- **Free Entry:** No charges for anyone

### Best Time to Visit

- **Morning:** 9:00 AM – 11:00 AM (peaceful, good lighting for photos)
- **Afternoon:** 2:00 PM – 4:00 PM (cooler hours)
- **Evening:** 5:00 PM – 6:30 PM (sunset views)
- **Closed:** Mondays

### Entry Fee

- **Free** for everyone (no entry charge)
- **Donations** accepted at the entrance

### Lotus Temple Nearest Metro Station and Exit Gate Summary

The **Lotus Temple nearest metro station and exit gate** is Kalkaji Mandir Gate 2. This is one of the most **Instagram-worthy Delhi Metro tourist places**.

### Why Lotus Temple Is Perfect for Metro Tourists

The **Lotus Temple nearest metro station and exit gate** makes this spiritual site accessible. Combined with **Magenta Line** connectivity, it's a top choice for **Delhi sightseeing by metro**.

## 5. Chandni Chowk Market & Jama Masjid

> Historic Market & Mughal Mosque

![Chandni Chowk crowded market street with food stalls](/assets/images/blog/Chandni%20Chowk%20crowded%20market%20street%20with%20food%20stalls.jpg "Chandni Chowk crowded market street with food stalls")

**Chandni Chowk** is Delhi's oldest and busiest market, famous for street food, fabrics, jewelry, and traditional Delhi culture. Adjacent **Jama Masjid** is India's largest mosque.

| Detail | Information |
| **Nearest Metro Station** | [**Chandni Chowk Metro Station**](https://metroguideindia.com/delhi-metro/stations/chandni-chowk.html) (Yellow Line) |
| **Best Exit Gate for Market** | **Gate No. 3** (directly into main market) |
| **Best Exit Gate for Jama Masjid** | **Gate No. 4** (towards mosque side) |
| **Walking Distance to Market** | 2-minute walk (150 meters), **walking distance**! |
| **Walking Distance to Jama Masjid** | 8-minute walk (650 meters) |
| **Metro Line** | Yellow Line (Samaypur Badli to R.K. Puram) |
| **Quick Tip** | **Chandni Chowk metro station exit gate for market** is Gate 3, which drops you right in the middle of Paranthe Wali Gali and street food. Gate 4 is better for Jama Masjid. |

### Step-by-Step Walking Directions

### For Chandni Chowk Market (from Gate 3)

1. Exit through **Gate No. 3** at Chandni Chowk metro station
2. You're already in the **main market area**
3. Explore Paranthe Wali Gali, Dariba Kalan, and Kinari Bazaar
4. **2-minute walk** from gate to market entrance

### For Jama Masjid (from Gate 4)

1. Exit through **Gate No. 4** at Chandni Chowk metro station
2. Walk straight towards **Jama Masjid direction**
3. Cross the street at pedestrian signal
4. Walk 650 meters (8 minutes)
5. Jama Masjid main entrance will be ahead

### Must-Try Food in Chandni Chowk

| Food | Best Shop | Price |
| **Parathas** | Paranthe Wali Gali (100+ shops) | ₹50–₹150 |
| **Chaat** | Swami Namdar Chaat | ₹40–₹80 |
| **Jalebi** | Gurdas Ram Jalebi Wala | ₹30–₹60 |
| **Nihari** | NAT Nihari | ₹100–₹200 |
| **Ice Cream** | Bikaner Sweets | ₹40–₹80 |

### Best Time to Visit

- **Market:** 10:00 AM – 8:00 PM (shops open)
- **Jama Masjid:** 7:00 AM – 12:00 PM, 2:00 PM – 6:00 PM (avoid prayer times)
- **Food:** Evening (5:00 PM – 9:00 PM) for best street food experience

### Entry Fee

- **Chandni Chowk Market:** Free
- **Jama Masjid:** Free (₹300 for tourists to climb minaret)
- **Dress Code:** Modest clothing for Jama Masjid (shoulders & knees covered)

### Chandni Chowk Metro Station Exit Gate for Market Summary

The **Chandni Chowk metro station exit gate for market** is Gate 3, the most convenient **place to visit near metro stations** for foodies and shoppers.

## 6. Humayun's Tomb

> UNESCO World Heritage Site & Mughal Garden

![Humayun's Tomb with garden and reflecting pool](/assets/images/blog/Humayun%27s%20Tomb%20with%20garden%20and%20reflecting%20pool.jpg "Humayun's Tomb with garden and reflecting pool")

**Humayun's Tomb** is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and inspiration for the Taj Mahal. This Mughal garden tomb is one of the **best tourist places in Delhi** and perfectly maintained.

| Detail | Information |
| **Nearest Metro Station** | [**JLN Stadium Metro Station**](https://metroguideindia.com/delhi-metro/stations/jln-stadium.html) (Violet Line) |
| **Best Exit Gate** | **Gate No. 1** (towards Humayun's Tomb) |
| **Walking Distance** | 12-minute walk (1 km) |
| **Alternative Gate** | Gate No. 2 (15-minute walk, towards India Gate side) |
| **Metro Line** | Violet Line (Kashmere Gate to Raja Nahar Singh) |
| **Quick Tip** | Exit Gate 1, auto stands available (₹50–₹80) if walking is too long. The **walking distance** is manageable but hot in summer. |

### Step-by-Step Walking Directions from Gate 1

1. Exit through **Gate No. 1** at JLN Stadium metro station
2. Walk straight towards **INA Market direction**
3. Cross the road at pedestrian signal
4. Walk 1 km along the main road
5. You'll see Humayun's Tomb entrance on your right
6. **Auto stands** available if you prefer not to walk

### What to See Inside Humayun's Tomb

- **Main Tomb:** Beautiful Mughal architecture, red sandstone
- **Gardens:** Charbagh (four-quarter garden) design
- **Nila Gumbad:** Nearby blue-domed tomb
- **Tomb of Isa Khan:** Adjacent heritage structure
- **Reflecting Pool:** Perfect for photos

### Best Time to Visit

- **Morning:** 7:00 AM – 9:00 AM (cooler, soft light for photos)
- **Evening:** 4:00 PM – 6:00 PM (beautiful sunset)
- **Avoid:** Midday (11 AM – 3 PM) due to heat

### Entry Fee

- **Indian Citizens:** ₹50
- **Foreign Tourists:** ₹550
- **Children below 15:** Free
- **Photography:** Free (no tripod charge)

### Why Humayun's Tomb Is Perfect for Metro Tourists

Though slightly farther (**12-minute walk**), Humayun's Tomb is one of the most **picturesque Delhi Metro tourist places**. The **Violet Line** connects you directly from central Delhi.

## 7. Connaught Place & Rajiv Chowk

> Delhi's Premier Shopping & Dining Hub

![Connaught Place colonial architecture with metro station](/assets/images/blog/Connaught%20Place%20colonial%20architecture%20with%20metro%20station.jpg "Connaught Place colonial architecture with metro station")

**Connaught Place (CP)** and **Rajiv Chowk** are at the heart of Delhi's commercial and shopping scene. This colonial-era market is perfect for **budget travel** and **Delhi sightseeing by metro**.

| Detail | Information |
| **Nearest Metro Station** | [**Rajiv Chowk Metro Station**](https://metroguideindia.com/delhi-metro/stations/rajiv-chowk.html) (Yellow Line + Blue Line) |
| **Best Exit Gate** | **Gate No. 1** (towards Inner Circle/CP) |
| **Alternative Gate** | Gate No. 2 (Outer Circle), Gate No. 3 (Palika Bazaar) |
| **Walking Distance** | 3-minute walk (250 meters), **walking distance**! |
| **Metro Line** | Yellow Line + Blue Line (confluence point) |
| **Quick Tip** | Places at walking distance from Rajiv Chowk include CP, Palika Bazaar, Janpath Market, and India Gate. Gate 1 is best for inner circle shopping. |

### Step-by-Step Walking Directions from Gate 1

1. Exit through **Gate No. 1** at [Rajiv Chowk metro station](https://metroguideindia.com/blog/rajiv-chowk-yellow-blue-line-interchange-guide)
2. You're already in **Connaught Place**
3. Inner Circle: High-end shops, cafes, restaurants
4. Outer Circle: Budget shopping, street food
5. **Palika Bazaar:** Underground market (Gate 3)

### What to Do in Connaught Place

- **Shopping:** Inner Circle (brand stores), Outer Circle (budget)
- **Food:** 100+ restaurants, cafes, street food
- **Palika Bazaar:** Underground electronics market (Gate 3)
- **Janpath Market:** Tourist handicrafts, clothes (Gate 2)
- **India Gate:** 15-minute walk or Yulu bike from CP

### Best Time to Visit

- **Morning:** 10:00 AM – 12:00 PM (shops open, less crowded)
- **Evening:** 6:00 PM – 9:00 PM (best shopping, dining, nightlife)
- **Night:** 9:00 PM – 11:00 PM (cafes, restaurants)

### Entry Fee

- **Free** (public area)
- Individual shops/restaurants have their own prices

### Places at Walking Distance from Rajiv Chowk

| Attraction | Walking Time |
| Connaught Place Inner Circle | 3 minutes |
| Palika Bazaar | 5 minutes |
| Janpath Market | 5 minutes |
| India Gate | 15 minutes / 5-minute Yulu ride |
| India Gate (via Kartavya Path) | 20 minutes |

### Why Connaught Place Is Perfect for Metro Tourists

**Rajiv Chowk** is the **largest metro station in India** and the confluence of Yellow + Blue Lines. This makes it the **best Delhi Metro route for tourists** starting point. **Places at walking distance from Rajiv Chowk** include most major attractions.

## 8. Qutub Minar

> UNESCO World Heritage Site & Tallest Minaret

![Qutub Minar tower with metro station in background](/assets/images/blog/Qutub%20Minar%20tower%20with%20metro%20station%20in%20background.jpg "Qutub Minar tower with metro station in background")

**Qutub Minar** is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the tallest brick minaret in the world (73 meters). This **Delhi tourist place near Yellow Line metro** is a must-visit for history lovers.

| Detail | Information |
| **Nearest Metro Station** | [**Qutub Minar Metro Station**](https://metroguideindia.com/delhi-metro/stations/qutab-minar.html) (Yellow Line) |
| **Best Exit Gate** | **Gate No. 1** (directly towards monument entrance) |
| **Walking Distance** | 8-minute walk (700 meters) |
| **Alternative Gate** | Gate No. 2 (10-minute walk, towards parking) |
| **Metro Line** | Yellow Line (Samaypur Badli to R.K. Puram) |
| **Quick Tip** | Exit Gate 1, you'll see Qutub Minar clearly. **Auto stands** available (₹40–₹60) if walking is too long. |

### Step-by-Step Walking Directions from Gate 1

1. Exit through **Gate No. 1** at Qutub Minar metro station
2. Walk straight towards the monument (clearly visible)
3. Cross the road at pedestrian signal
4. Walk 700 meters on the dedicated footpath
5. Qutub Minar entrance will be directly ahead

### What to See Inside Qutub Complex

- **Qutub Minar:** 73-meter tall minaret (climb for ₹30)
- **Iron Pillar:** 7-meter tall, 6th-century rust-resistant pillar
- **Alai Darwaza:** Beautiful red sandstone gateway
- **Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque:** India's first mosque (1193)
- **Scientific Museum:** Small museum on-site

### Best Time to Visit

- **Morning:** 8:00 AM – 10:00 AM (cooler, good light)
- **Evening:** 4:00 PM – 6:00 PM (beautiful sunset)
- **Light & Sound Show:** 7:00 PM (₹60)

### Entry Fee

- **Indian Citizens:** ₹40
- **Foreign Tourists:** ₹550
- **Children below 15:** Free
- **Climb Minar:** Additional ₹30

### Why Qutub Minar Is Perfect for Metro Tourists

The **Qutub Minar nearest metro station** is literally named after it! This is one of the most **accessible Delhi tourist places near Yellow Line metro**.

## 9. Akshardham Gardens & National Heritage Art Complex

> Cultural Complex & Musical Fountain

![Akshardham Gardens ](/assets/images/blog/Akshardham%20Gardens.jpg "Akshardham Gardens with musical fountain show")

**Akshardham Gardens** (separate from the temple) is a beautiful cultural complex with musical fountains, exhibitions, and gardens. Great for **budget travel** and family outings.

| Detail | Information |
| **Nearest Metro Station** | **Akshardham Metro Station** (Blue Line) |
| **Best Exit Gate** | **Gate No. 2** (towards gardens) |
| **Walking Distance** | 5-minute walk (400 meters) |
| **Alternative Gate** | Gate No. 1 (3-minute walk, temple entrance) |
| **Metro Line** | Blue Line (Dwarka Sector 21 to Noida Electronic City) |
| **Quick Tip** | **Tourist attractions on Delhi Metro Blue Line** include both temple and gardens. Gate 2 is best for gardens only. |

### What to See in Akshardham Gardens

- **Musical Fountain:** Evening show (₹80)
- **Gandhi Kennedy Exhibition:** Inspirational journey
- **Yajnakund:** Fire ritual demonstration
- **Gardens:** Beautifully landscaped, perfect for photos
- **Boat Ride:** Historical journey through India (₹60)

### Best Time to Visit

- **Evening:** 5:00 PM – 8:00 PM (fountain show at 7:00 PM)
- **Avoid:** Midday (heat)

### Entry Fee

- **Gardens:** Free
- **Musical Fountain:** ₹80 adults, ₹40 children
- **Boat Ride:** ₹60 adults, ₹30 children

### Why Akshardham Gardens Is Perfect for Metro Tourists

**Tourist attractions on Delhi Metro Blue Line** include both temple and gardens. The **Akshardham metro station** makes this **walking distance** experience perfect for families.

## 10. India Gate Night View & Kartavya Path

> Illuminated Monument & Evening Stroll

![India Gate lit up at night with Kartavya Path](/assets/images/blog/India%20Gate%20lit%20up%20at%20night%20with%20Kartavya%20Path.webp "India Gate lit up at night with Kartavya Path")

**India Gate at night** is magical, fully illuminated with the newly renovated **Kartavya Path** making it perfect for evening walks. This is one of the best **Delhi sightseeing by metro** experiences.

| Detail | Information |
| **Nearest Metro Station** | **Central Secretariat Metro Station** (Yellow Line + Violet Line) |
| **Best Exit Gate** | **Gate No. 3** (towards Kartavya Path) |
| **Walking Distance** | 10-minute walk (800 meters) |
| **Metro Line** | Yellow Line + Violet Line |
| **Quick Tip** | Visit **after 6:00 PM** for best illumination. **Yulu bikes** available at Gate 3 (₹20–₹40). |

### Best Time to Visit

- **Evening:** 6:00 PM – 9:00 PM (best illumination, cooler weather)
- **Night:** 9:00 PM – 10:00 PM (less crowded, romantic)

### Entry Fee

- **Free** (no entry charge)

### Why India Gate Night View Is Perfect for Metro Tourists

The **nearest metro station to India Gate with gate number** is Central Secretariat Gate 3. This is one of the most **Instagram-worthy Delhi Metro tourist places**.

## Delhi Metro Route for Tourists: Best Lines to Use

### Yellow Line - Top Tourist Attractions

The **Yellow Line** connects the most **Delhi tourist places near Yellow Line metro**:

## Money-Saving Tips for Delhi Metro Tourists

### 1. Use Smart Card for 10% Discount

- **10% off** all fares
- **₹150 cost** (₹50 refundable + ₹100 initial load)
- **Pays for itself** in 2–3 weeks of regular use

### 2. Travel on Sundays for Discounted Fares

- **₹10–₹11 savings** per journey
- Maximum fare on Sunday: **₹54** (vs ₹64 weekday)

### 3. Use Yulu Bikes for Last-Mile Connectivity

- **₹20–₹40** for short rides
- Available at most metro stations
- Perfect for 1–2 km walks

### 4. Avoid Autos for Short Distances

- **Auto rates:** ₹50–₹150 for 1–3 km
- **Metro + walk:** ₹11–₹64 for same distance
- **Save ₹100+ per trip**

### 5. Plan Your Route to Minimize Interchanges

- Each interchange adds 5–10 minutes
- **Yellow Line + Blue Line** covers most attractions
- **Violet Line** adds Lotus Temple, Humayun's Tomb
